registeredBy: Sam (owner) chose to pre-register G25 before the tool is built (efficient build order, 2026-11-09); registered before any run and before the runner exists
plannedStep: G25 Yield curve and financial conditions
hypothesis: A calendar year in which a country's average 10-year government bond yield is below its average central bank policy rate (an inverted curve; Estrella and Mishkin 1998) is followed by a fall in real GDP the next calendar year more often than years in general.

params.spread: annual average 10-year yield minus annual average policy rate
params.outcome: real GDP growth below 0 in year t+1

data.signal: 10-year yields as the app reads them (FRED IRLTLT01 series and national sources already on file) and BIS central bank policy rates
data.outcome: IMF World Economic Outlook real GDP growth (NGDP_RPCH), outturn years only, never projections
data.universe: Every country with at least 15 years of both a 10-year yield and a policy rate

knownLimits: Annual data: an inversion late in year t and a recession early in t+1 count, but one that leads by more than two years does not. A quarterly test would need quarterly GDP for every country and is not planned.
A fall in annual real GDP is a stricter test than a dated recession (NBER or CEPR style); short recessions inside a growing year are missed.
Growth figures are today's WEO vintage, not what was known at the time; the yield and the policy rate are not revised.
The policy rate stands in for a 3-month bill rate, which the app does not hold for most countries. Where policy rates were capped at zero, the spread reads steeper than market rates would show.
Only a pass lets the app show a recession probability; that probability is then the historical hit rate of this rule, not a fitted probit.
